decisions.evidence: R1 maker: baseline spec described a 'focused v1' where, per client's reading, 'I have to type the title myself and the app won't pull anything from the page' — i.e. no automatic metadata collection (violates REF-BM-02/03). R1 client: 'Could you make it so that when I paste a link, the app automatically grabs the page's title and description, and I can still edit them if I want?' R2 maker delivered it: 'Pasting a valid public link automatically fetches its page title and description... editable before and after saving.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Reference divergence established independently: the round-1 spec omitted auto-collection of page metadata. Client rejects the mismatch and supplies the reference-conforming behaviour (auto-fetch title+description, still editable) → corrective, catch_type=correct.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker: 'Accounts, device sync, sharing, imports, and browser extensions are excluded for now.' R1 client: 'Everything else in here — tags, search, filtering, editing, and the delete-with-confirmation — is fine for a first version, so this is the one change I'm asking for.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Importing bookmarks (REF-BM-30, Netscape HTML) is an extended reference item explicitly presented as excluded → divergence. Client gives bare blanket approval of 'everything else' without naming imports or expressing the difference → unexpressed. (Accounts/device-sync/sharing/browser-extensions are infra REF-BM-I01/I02/I04 or non-reference, excluded as orthogonal.)

decisions.evidence: R2 maker: 'automatically fetches its page title and description' — only title+description. R5 maker delivery: 'Automatic title and description retrieval'. R5 client: item 'showed up with its title, description, tags, and date' — no favicon/preview. Client (R2): 'filling in the title and description ... matches what I had in mind.'
decisions.note: Specification/implementation review, same REF item at a later point than decision 1. REF-BM-02 also requires favicon and preview image; the presented and delivered retrieval covers only title+description → partial divergence. Client restates only title/description and never mentions favicon/preview → unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: R5 client (implementation review): 'it caught a duplicate when I tried saving the same link twice and pointed me to the existing one'. R5 maker delivery listed save/revisit flow.
decisions.note: Implementation review. Duplicate-URL handling guiding to the existing bookmark conforms to REF-BM-06; recorded conforming decision surfaced at delivery.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker: 'save/find/edit/delete flow'; R5 client: 'I saved a bookmark and it showed up with its title, description, tags, and date'.
decisions.note: Save a bookmark by url conforms to REF-BM-01. Recorded conforming decision.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker included 'editing'; R5 client: 'editing updated the saved values'.
decisions.note: Editing a bookmark conforms to REF-BM-04. Recorded conforming decision.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker: 'confirmed deletion'; R5 client: 'deleting asked for confirmation and then removed it cleanly.'
decisions.note: Delete a bookmark conforms to REF-BM-05; confirmation is an equivalent UI choice, not a divergence. Recorded conforming decision.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker: 'tags'; R5 client: bookmark 'showed up with its title, description, tags'.
decisions.note: Assigning tags conforms to REF-BM-09. Recorded conforming decision. (Tag autocomplete REF-BM-10 was never presented, so not a decision here.)

decisions.evidence: R1 maker: 'filtering'; R5 client: 'search and tag filtering both narrowed things down correctly'.
decisions.note: Filtering to a tag's bookmarks conforms to REF-BM-11. Recorded conforming decision.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker: 'search'; R5 client: 'search ... narrowed things down correctly'.
decisions.note: Generic full-text search conforms to REF-BM-12 at the presented level. Advanced search semantics (case-insensitivity REF-BM-13, #tag REF-BM-14, boolean/parentheses REF-BM-15, phrase REF-BM-16) were never presented in detail, so they are coverage gaps judged separately, not presented divergent decisions.
